/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:70:## Decision 5 — Automatic page metadata (title, description, favicon, preview) — collected **before** commit
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-71-
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-72-- **Decision**: Metadata is collected **synchronously, up front, for the person to
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-73-  review and edit before the bookmark is committed** (matching spec US1 scenario 1).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-74-  The flow is two steps:
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:75:  1. **Prepare/preview** (no persistence): given the URL, fetch the target with a
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-76-     plain HTTP request (short, bounded timeout — see below) and parse the returned
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-77-     HTML with Cheerio for `<title>`, meta description / `og:description`, `og:image`
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:78:     (preview), and favicon (`<link rel="icon">`, fallback `/favicon.ico`). Resolve
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-79-     relative asset URLs to absolute. Return these for review.
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-80-  2. **Commit**: the person reviews/edits title and description, then saves; the
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-81-     **reviewed values are what get persisted**.
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-82-- **Fetch timeout / fallback**: the prepare fetch uses a bounded timeout (target
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:83:  ~8s, comfortably inside the 15s save budget of SC-001). If the page cannot be read
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-84-  promptly (timeout, offline, blocked), prepare returns **fallback details**
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-85-  (title derived from the page/host, empty description) so the person can continue
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-86-  and save immediately, then edit later (FR-007).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-87-- **Rationale**: A simple GET + Cheerio is fast enough to fit inside the save
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-88-  budget while giving the person the automatically collected details to confirm or
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-89-  change before committing — the experience the client approved. Only the slower
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:90:  snapshot capture is deferred to the background (Decision 6/11).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-91-- **Alternatives considered**: Collecting metadata asynchronously after create —
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-92-  **rejected**: it hides the details until after commit and contradicts the
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-93-  approved "review before saving" experience. Rendering every page in Chromium for
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-94-  metadata — slower/heavier than needed; reserve Chromium for snapshots.
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-95-  Third-party metadata APIs — external dependency and privacy cost for a local app.

/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:174:## Decision 11 — What runs in the background (snapshot only) & the no-overwrite rule
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-175-
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:176:- **Decision**: The **only** background work is snapshot capture (Decision 6).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-177-  Metadata is resolved before commit (Decision 5), so creating a bookmark persists
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:178:  the reviewed title/description/favicon/preview immediately, then enqueues snapshot
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-179-  capture in a lightweight in-process queue that updates `snapshotStatus`
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-180-  (`pending` → `available`/`unavailable`).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-181-- **No-overwrite rule (hard constraint)**: Background jobs MUST NEVER modify the
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-182-  `title` or `description` of a bookmark. Snapshot capture writes only
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-183-  `snapshotType`, `snapshotStatus`, and `snapshotPath` (and, only if still empty,
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:184:  `faviconPath`/`previewImagePath`). This guarantees that any value the person
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:185:  entered or edited is never clobbered by later background work (client requirement).
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-186-- **Rationale**: Keeps save fast for the person while honoring "review details
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-187-  before commit"; capturing a self-contained snapshot can be slow, so it is the
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:188:  only thing deferred. Restricting background writes to snapshot-related fields is
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-189-  the simplest robust way to make overwrites structurally impossible.

/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md:192:  needed; simply forbidding background writes to title/description is safer and
/presentation/round-05/001-bookmark-manager__research.md-193-  clearer. Doing snapshots synchronously on save — would blow the 15s budget on
